title: Enforce the continuation nudge on agent_settled, gated on the block verdict
action: The belt calls session-close on agent_settled and throws its return value away, so the one verdict that is meant to force the session onward is dropped. Fix that. Capture the helper's stdout, parse it, and act ONLY on the block-decision shape — read adapter.rs to learn the two shapes the rule can emit, because the ordinary advisory shape is also non-empty and treating any non-empty output as a nudge would force a turn on every routine reminder for every user. That is the single highest-consequence mistake available in this cell. When and only when the block shape is present, inject its reason through pi.sendUserMessage per 663c642e — not pi.sendMessage, whose custom messages want a renderer that D2 forbids, and which the live test harness does not stub. Reuse the belt's existing injection discipline rather than inventing a second one: it already has a capability guard for that API and its own busy and in-flight latches. Await the call inside try/catch so no floating promise escapes as an unhandled rejection, and make sure nothing you start outlives the session. You do not need your own repeat guard — the Rust side already dedupes this verdict on a session-stable key inside a time window; read that code so you can say why, and cite it in the comment rather than adding a second latch. Then extend the live test harness with whatever you assert on: the stub Pi object and stub context must expose the surfaces your probes touch, and the stub bee must be able to return both emitted shapes, or the probes pass without proving anything. Add probes that an ordinary advisory nudge does NOT trigger a turn, that the block shape DOES, and that a failure in the injection is swallowed rather than thrown.

truths: Only the block-decision shape triggers a turn; an ordinary advisory message never does, and a probe asserts that negative case
The injection uses pi.sendUserMessage per 663c642e and reuses the belt's existing capability guard and latches
No floating promise: a failed injection is caught and logged, never thrown
The test harness exposes every surface the new probes assert on, so no probe can pass vacuously
The handler stays advisory and fail-open; the blocking path is untouched
